extraction.name: VAP-Data
extraction.description: A synthetic paired-video dataset for semantic-controlled video generation, containing over 100K samples across 100 semantic conditions in four categories: concept, style, motion, and camera movement. Reference and target videos share non-pixel-aligned semantic controls.
extraction.license: The authors state that any artifact release will be accompanied by a research-only license and an acceptable-use policy explicitly prohibiting abusive or unlawful scenarios; a specific license is not provided.
extraction.creator: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, and Qiang Xu
extraction.citeAs: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, and Qiang Xu. Video-As-Prompt: Unified Semantic Control for Video Generation. arXiv:2510.20888v1, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors collected 2K high-quality reference images from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. They used Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models, including VIDU and Kling, and community LoRAs to generate paired videos by matching each image to all compatible templates. Some templates restrict subject categories. Appendix D additionally describes commercial APIs, including PixVerse, as part of the automated generation engine.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: High-quality real reference images collected from the Internet. Synthetic videos were generated using commercial visual-effects templates and APIs from VIDU, Kling, and PixVerse, together with community visual-effects LoRAs from Civitai.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reference images were matched to compatible Image-to-Video visual-effects templates and community LoRAs to generate videos. Reference and target videos were paired according to shared semantic controls, without requiring pixel-wise correspondence.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For model training, videos were resized to 480 × 720 (832), and 49 frames were sampled at 16 fps. Reference and target videos and their first frames were encoded into latents using a video VAE; captions were encoded using a text encoder.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Semantic-condition subset names come from commercial-model API definitions and community visual-effects LoRA definitions. Conditions were organized into concept, style, motion, and camera movement categories. Reference and target videos have standard video-description captions that help identify their shared semantic control signals; the paper does not specify how those captions were authored.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The collected reference images include men, women, and children. Semantic-condition subsets include gender swap, child memory, and selfie with younger self. The paper does not describe separately collected demographic metadata.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The intended applications are research, education, and creative prototyping. Identified misuse risks include identity impersonation, deepfakes, targeted harassment, deceptive political messaging, and sexualized or violent media. Proposed mitigations include a research-only release, an acceptable-use policy prohibiting abusive or unlawful scenarios, and default content filters blocking clearly harmful categories such as sexual content, explicit violence, and hate symbols.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Because the dataset is synthetic and derived from commercial visual-effects templates and community LoRAs, it may transmit the source models' stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations. For example, poor hand generation in source models may prevent VAP from learning to generate hands well from this data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The semantic conditions are relatively limited, synthetic, and derived from other generative models rather than real-world paired video collection. The data may inherit source-template artifacts and conceptual limitations. Standard video-description captions can inaccurately describe semantics, and mismatched descriptions or large structural differences between reference and target subjects can reduce semantic alignment and generation quality. Constructing larger-scale, real-world semantic-controlled video data is left to future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and testing unified semantic-controlled video generation models across concept, style, motion, and camera controls. The final VAP model uses 100K training pairs. Evaluation uses 48 test samples: two samples for each of 24 semantic conditions evenly sampled across the four categories. Intended use is research, education, and creative prototyping; surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, and other high-risk deployments are not intended uses.
